newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil minister says CVRD sale on for Q1.
newsitem.headline: Brazil minister says CVRD sale on for Q1.

text.p: Brazilian Planning Minister Antonio Kandir Tuesday reaffirmed the government's intention to kick off in the first quarter of 1997 the privatization of state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD).
A spokeswoman for the minister said Kandir had rejected a newspaper report claiming CVRD had made a "historic" new gold and copper find in Carajas in Para state.
"The minister affirmed that the process of privatization of CVRD will not be thrown offcourse by this (report)," the spokeswoman told Reuters.

The O Estado de Sao Paulo daily Tuesday, citing unnamed sources in the Presidential Palace, said the company had made the new finds near the existing Igarape Bahia gold mine and the Salobo gold, copper and silver project.

CVRD officials quickly denied the report, saying it was a repeat of a speculative news story in October. The company said it was continuing to survey the area mentioned and added it was still too early to evaluate the mineral content.
Traders in the Sao Paulo stock exchange feared the report could whip up further opposition to the CVRD selloff.
